newsItems.title: Muchova and Noskova Set All-Czech Wimbledon Final as Men's Semis Await
newsItems.excerpt: Wimbledon 2026 delivered a historic women's semi-final day on Thursday before attention turned to Friday's men's last-four clashes on Centre Court. Karolina Muchova saved a match point and survived a 12-10 third-set tie-break to defeat Coco Gauff 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (12-10) in two hours and 35 minutes, reaching her second Grand Slam final after the 2023 French Open. Linda Noskova followed with a composed 6-4, 6-4 victory over Marta Kostyuk, guaranteeing the first all-Czech women's Wimbledon final since the Open era began and the first same-nation women's title match at SW19 since Serena and Venus Williams met in 2009. On the men's side, British wildcard Arthur Fery — ranked No. 114 and only the fifth British man in the Open era to reach a Wimbledon semi-final — faces Roland Garros champion Alexander Zverev at 1:30pm BST, with defending champion Jannik Sinner meeting seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic in the evening semi-final. Sinner leads their head-to-head 6-5 but Djokovic won their Australian Open semi-final in January. Great Britain's Henry Patten and Harri Heliovaara also reached the men's doubles final, while Alfie Hewett advanced to the wheelchair singles semi-finals.

newsItems.title: Wei Chong and Wooi Yik Launch New Malaysia Doubles Era at Japan Open
newsItems.excerpt: The DAIHATSU Japan Open, a BWF World Tour Super 750 event with a $950,000 prize purse, begins July 14 at the Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium and will mark the competitive debut of Malaysia's reshuffled men's doubles pairing of Man Wei Chong and Olympic bronze medallist Soh Wooi Yik. National coach Herry IP has been testing several new combinations ahead of the Asian Games cycle, and the scratch pair face a demanding opener against Taiwan's world No. 18 duo Lee Fang Chih and Lee Fang Jen, with a potential second-round clash against either France's Popov brothers or Indonesia's second seeds Fajar Alfian and Muhammad Shohibul Fikri awaiting the winner. Indonesia has confirmed a 12-player delegation across all disciplines, leaning on three men's doubles pairs as its primary strength, while Jonatan Christie and Alwi Farhan lead the singles charge. Reigning men's doubles champions Goh Sze Fei and Nur Izzuddin Rumsani open against China's Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi, and world No. 5 Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan begin against Taiwan's Hsu Yin Hui and Lin Jhih Yun. The tournament arrives days after the Badminton Association of Malaysia became the first body in the region to deploy an AI-powered Instant Review System at the AFFIN 100PLUS Junior Elite Tour Finals.

newsItems.title: PPA Tour Turns to Melbourne and Singapore After Tokyo Open Surge
newsItems.excerpt: Professional pickleball's international calendar accelerates this week after Hong Kit Wong's dominant Sansan Tokyo Open run, where the world No. 15 captured his third PPA Tour Asia singles title without dropping a game. The Carvana PPA Tour's July slate opens with the PPA Australia 250 Melbourne from July 15 to 19, one of the circuit's highest-ranked events in the Southern Hemisphere this summer, followed by the Macon PPA Challenger in Georgia from July 17 to 19 for aspiring pros chasing ranking points. Tama Shimabukuro's Tokyo doubles and mixed doubles titles and Mitchell Hargreaves' 15-place singles ranking jump to No. 24 underscore the depth of competition across the Asia swing. Attention then shifts to the Leapmotor PPA Asia 500 Singapore Open from July 23 to 26 at The Sports Arina @ Expo — the first PPA Tour Asia event staged in Singapore with a $70,000 purse — before the PPA Italy 125 Portoroz runs July 22 to 26. The 2026-2027 global season officially resumes August 31 with the Veolia Pickleball National Championships, while the PPA Asia calendar also features Shenzhen in August and the $1.1 million Hong Kong Slam in October.

newsItems.title: Sun Yingsha Claims Sixth Grand Smash Title as Brazil Stage Looms
newsItems.excerpt: Sun Yingsha added another milestone to her dominant 2026 season by edging compatriot Kuai Man 4-3 in an all-China women's singles final at the WTT United States Smash in Ontario, California, prevailing 11-9, 11-6, 9-11, 11-5, 7-11, 10-12, 11-4 to claim her sixth career Grand Smash title and second of the year. The 25-year-old world champion said staying focused through the deciding game represented a major step forward, while Kuai reflected on a breakthrough run that included doubles gold alongside Wang Manyu. On the men's side, Japan's Sora Matsushima captured singles gold after a tournament that saw defending champion Wang Chuqin eliminated by Denmark's Anders Lind in the round of 16 and Lin Shidong fall to France's Alexis Lebrun, ending China's men's singles campaign before the quarter-finals. China still swept both doubles titles as Wen Ruibo and Yuan Licen won men's doubles and Wang Manyu and Kuai Man took the women's crown. The World Table Tennis calendar now shifts to the WTT Star Contender Brazil from July 21 to 26 in São José dos Campos — the first Star Contender staged in São Paulo state at Vale Sul Shopping — where home hope Hugo Calderano, the defending champion from Foz do Iguaçu 2025, and world No. 23 Bruna Takahashi headline a field of more than 80 international players.
